data.name: Nicolae
data.gender_notes: Nicolae is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Nicolae is derived from the Latin word 'Nicolaos', which comes from the Greek 'nikē' (victory) and 'laos' (people). It is a name that signifies a victorious or conqueror. In Christianity, Saint Nicholas is the patron saint of this name, known for his generosity and charitable deeds. The name Nicolae carries the meaning “Victor, Conqueror” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Nicolae usually hope their child will grow to embody victor, conqueror and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for those who have overcome great challenges and have emerged victorious in their spiritual lives.
data.etymology: Nicolae belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Victor, Conqueror.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nicolae total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_hebrew.name: ניקולא
in_hebrew.long_meaning: ניקולא הוא שם שמקורו ביוונית וניקרא על שם ניקולאוס הקדוש. הוא מורכב משני מילים: 'ניקאו' (נίκη) שמשמעותו 'נצחון' ו-'לאוס' (λαός) שמשמעותו 'עם'. השם ניקולא מתורגם כ'נצחון העם' או 'מנצח את העם'. השם ניקולא הוא מקורו של השם ניקולאי ויש לו משמעות רבה במסורת הנוצרית והקתולית.

in_greek.name: Νικόλαος
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Νικόλαος είναι ένα όνομα που προέρχεται από την ελληνική γλώσσα και σημαίνει 'νίκη του λαού' ή 'αυτός που νικάει τον λαό'. Το όνομα αποτελείται από δύο λέξεις: 'νίκη' (nikē) που σημαίνει 'νίκη' και 'λαός' (laos) που σημαίνει 'λαός' ή 'πληθυσμός'. Το όνομα Νικόλαος ήταν πολύ δημοφιλές στην αρχαία Ελλάδα και συνδέεται με τον Άγιο Νικόλαο, έναν από τους πιο δημοφιλείς αγίους της Ορθόδοξης Εκκλησίας.

in_latin.name: Nicolae
in_latin.long_meaning: Nicolae nomen habet origine Graeca et significat 'victoriam populi' vel 'qui populum vincit'. Nomen constat ex duobus verbis: 'nike' (victoria) et 'laos' (populus). Sanctus Nicolaus, episcopus Myrensis, fuit vir sanctus et largus, qui saeculo IV floruit et veluti protector navium et puerorum habetur.

in_english.name: Nicolae
in_english.meaning: Victory of the people or conqueror of the people
in_english.long_meaning: The name Nicolae originates from the Greek name Nikolaos (Νικόλαος), meaning 'victory of the people' or 'conqueror of the people'. It is derived from two Greek words: 'nike' (victory) and 'laos' (people). The name has significant importance in Christian tradition, particularly associated with Saint Nicholas, a 4th-century bishop of Myra (modern-day Demre, Turkey), known for his generosity and kindness, especially towards children. The name Nicolae is popular in many Christian cultures and symbolizes triumph and leadership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Nicolae carries a strong cultural significance, as it is associated with the historical figure of Saint Nicholas, a popular and beloved saint in both the Eastern and Western Christian traditions. Known as the 'Wonderworker' or 'Blessed Protector', Nicolas was a fourth-century bishop in Myra, Lycia (present-day Turkey). He is remembered for his secret gift-giving and miraculous interventions, inspiring the later development of Santa Claus.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual sense, the name Nicolae represents the idea of triumph over hardships, struggles, and adversity. It is a reminder that, as Christians, we have the power and strength to overcome challenges through faith, perseverance, and the generosity and support of others. Saint Nicholas' life serves as a model of living a life guided by love, compassion, and charitable acts, demonstrating the transformative power of giving and receiving.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Nicolae is derived from the Greek name Nikolaos, meaning "victory of the people." In Christian tradition, St. Nicholas is the patron saint of children and sailors, symbolizing protection, love, and generosity.

historical_references.reference: Nicolae Copiaş, a Romanian Orthodox hieromonk and theologian, played a significant role in the Romanian Orthodox Church during the late 19th and early 20th centuries. He was born as Grigore Oantea in 1877 in the village of Pădureni in the Moldavia region. After his monastic tonure, he took the name Nicolae. He was a strong advocate for the Romanian language in liturgy and played a crucial role in translating the Romanian Orthodox Divine Liturgy into modern Romanian.

Nicolae Teclu, a Wallachian boyar and one of the most powerful and influential figures in the late 16th-century Principality of Wallachia, was known for his patronage of the arts and sciences. He was born around 1510 and took the name Nicolae upon his election as Prince in 1552. He was known for his efforts to modernize Wallachian society and his support for the arts, including the construction of the Curtea de Argeş Monastery.
